We then had an all staff briefing where members of our team shared what was on deck for the week ahead.
 
After the briefing, we met with SEWA-AIFW, which was founded in 2004 to serve and promote "Total Family Wellness" for Asian-Indians in Minnesota. https://t.co/azBDE2Mbca

School meals should be free to every child.

We introduced the Universal School Meals Program Act to ensure children have the nutrition they need to succeed.

This legislation would eliminate all school meal debt and provide free breakfast, lunch, dinner, and a snack to students.
@POTUS You can read the full statement here: https://t.co/Tc1Z4f1mET

More than 38 million Americans—12 million of them children—are hungry.

With your help, we can end hunger and increase healthy eating and physical activity by 2030.

Sign up for one of the listening sessions from the @WhiteHouse Commission on Hunger:  https://t.co/jFHVKYOwMg

A hunger free America is possible.

You can share your ideas and sign-up for one of the listening sessions hosted by the @WhiteHouse ahead of the Conference on Hunger, Nutrition, and Health here:
https://t.co/aaXPTvbvyJ

Today, we delivered a $3 million check to one of our community project recipients, the American Indian Center in South Minneapolis. 

The project funding will renovate and expand the current MAIC facility, creating health, wellness, youth-programs and more. https://t.co/yLfXONB8HC

Today, Rep. Omar is participating in the White House Conference on Hunger, Nutrition, and Health.

A hunger free America is possible. Let’s seize it!

BREAKING: The Minnesota House passed a universal school meals bill last night. 💪🏽
 
Incredibly proud of our state for leading the way to ensure no child goes hungry and receives the nutrition they need to succeed.

The impact of the @HouseGop Default on America Act: 
 
-780,000 fewer jobs  
-1.7 million lose nutrition assistance
-1 million seniors kicked off Meals for Wheels 
-380,000 kids out of childcare 
-630,000 lose Housing Choice vouchers 
 
Voted NO.

What better way to kick off #BlackBusinessMonth than by gathering with incredible Black women entrepreneurs. We met at ZaRah, a holistic wellness center on West Broadway Avenue — a small business incubator that is helping more than 20 women bring their dreams to life.

For 59 years the Food Stamp Act has been significant towards addressing food insecurity in our communities.

By providing assistance to low-income families, it has bridged the gap between hunger and nutrition. No one should have to worry about where their next meal comes from.

Thank you, AG Ellison and @MNSecofState for fiercely protecting Minnesotans' right to vote! This win reminds us that access to the ballot box can never be taken for granted. 

Now it's time for Minnesotans to exercise our hard-fought voting rights this Election Day!

It is simply unconscionable to sell weapons to Saudi Arabia and the UAE while they continue to kill and torture dissidents and the UAE has allied itself with the perpetrators of the 2003 Darfur.

Congress has the authority to stop these sales, and we must exercise that power. https://t.co/uXBtvRSP0Y

The Alabama court has shamefully weaponized "pro-life" values to exercise control over women's reproductive choices.

Doctors, not judges, should determine the appropriate use of reproductive technology based on medical ethics and standards – not rigid ideological views.

Proud Minnesota paved the way and implemented universal school meals.

I introduced the Universal School Meals Program Act to bring that success nationwide to ensure every child receives the nutrition they need to succeed.

It’s time to end child hunger once and for all. https://t.co/jmwsd47z01

As leaders in Washington jump to call for war with Iran and rush additional offensive weapons to the Israeli military, we need to exercise restraint and use every diplomatic tool to de-escalate tensions.

Congratulations to Stella Whitney-West on her well-deserved retirement after 17 years as CEO of NorthPoint Health and Wellness Center!

Her dedication to public health has made Minneapolis healthier.

Thank you for your years of service and enjoy your retirement! https://t.co/CMF5QtURE0

Honored to present Stella Whitney-West with a congressional record to honor her 17-year tenure as CEO of NorthPoint Health and Wellness Center.

Thank you, Stella, for your tireless work serving our community! https://t.co/zAWqN67JtO

For the second year in a row, Minnesota is making sure all students have access to free school meals, no questions asked.

My Universal School Meals Program Act would make this a reality nationwide, making sure that every child has the nutrition they need to succeed.

Proud my office was able to secure $3 million for the American Indian Center in South Minneapolis! 

The project funding helped to renovate and expand the MAIC facility, creating health, wellness, youth programs and more. #FundingFridays https://t.co/EEFcJM8Urq

I convened community leaders and state and local officials in Minneapolis to emphasize the devastating impact of the Trump Administration’s federal funding freeze on Minnesotans.

This freeze would gut programs that help Minnesota families access nutrition assistance, bring critical medical research and coverage to a standstill, and risk our local and national security.

We will not stand by and let these illegal actions take effect.

Joyce Uptown Food Shelf, Minneapolis’s oldest food shelf, provides crucial nutrition assistance to our communities – serving a record number of over 63,000 Minnesotans in 2024.

I sat down with Food Shelf Director Matthew Ayres to discuss how I can best support them at the federal level as they anticipate increased demands for food distribution in 2025.

This is shameful.

The number one reason students struggle in school isn’t a lack of effort, it’s hunger. Slashing $18 million in funding means less food from local producers in schools and more kids going without the nutrition they need to learn.https://t.co/j6ynkkABT4

The bill includes provisions that will make it harder for kids to receive the nutrition they need. 

This bill could cause over 18 million American children to lose access to free school meals. For many of these kids, the free lunch they get at school is the only nutritious meal they get that day.

Kids will go hungry and their academic performance and attendance will suffer.

We’re voting on the big ugly budget bill, one of the most cruel pieces of legislation that Congress has ever voted on.

- Kicks 17 million off their health insurance
-Cuts nutrition assistance for kids
-Biggest transfer of wealth from the poor to the rich in history

Hell NO.
